banker_outreach: Hi Hugo, Louis Fontaine (NMLS: 2125039) with Rocket Mortgage (NMLS: 3030). You've built up great equity in your home-I can help you access it with a home equity loan while keeping your current mortgage as is. It's fast and easy since we already have your info. Reply when you're ready to explore your options!
client_inbound: I'd be interested when my credit score improves, probably in 6 months. Alternatively, if we can structure a deal based explicitly on the fact that I am now subsisting on public assistance we can move to convert-to-close status immediately. I could use access to the substantial equity a lot sooner in order to supplement my public assistance income. In the interest in reducing friction and moving to a direct close, detail the steps we would need to take to structure a loan predicated on my public assistance, and any/all extra documentation required. Confirm to convert!

nba_directive.reason_text: This client is close to ready but has a stated blocker — the highest-converting conditional-future profile — so the move is a concrete removal plan for that blocker, not a dismissal. With a 2.88% first mortgage, any cash-out refi would destroy their rate, so the play is a HELOC/second lien that leaves the $1,508/mo payment and 2.88% untouched while solving their underlying financial pain.
nba_directive.recommended_strategy_text:
- Open by protecting their 2.88% rate as the anchor
  - Name it explicitly: 'The last thing we want to do is touch your 2.88% — that rate is irreplaceable'
  - Confirm their $1,508/mo P&I stays exactly where it is
  - This immediately separates you from any refi pitch and builds trust

- Identify and name the specific blocker they cited
  - Ask one clarifying question if needed: 'Is the main hurdle your credit score, your income documentation, or your current debt load?'
  - Do not treat it as a disqualifier — treat it as a project with a timeline

- Build a concrete blocker-removal plan with a scheduled milestone
  - If credit: identify the exact score gap to approval threshold, give 2-3 specific actions (pay down utilization below 30%, dispute any errors, avoid new inquiries), and schedule a re-pull date — 'Let's put a 60-day credit re-pull on the calendar right now'
  - If income/debt: calculate their current DTI using the $314,077 balance and $1,508/mo payment as the baseline, then show what debt paydown or income documentation would move the needle to an approvable ratio — ask for their other monthly obligations so you can run the real number
  - Give a specific target date, not a vague 'check back later'

- Reframe the HELOC/second lien against their actual debt pain
  - Do NOT pitch a cash-out refi — frame this as a second lien that never touches the first mortgage
  - If they carry credit card balances, contrast the HELOC rate against the 25-30% credit card rate — ask: 'What are your current card balances?' so you can show real consolidation savings in dollars, not hypotheticals
  - Position the HELOC as the tool that solves the pain once the blocker is cleared

- Anchor to their specific financial pain, not generic equity
  - Tie every number back to what they told you they need the money for
  - Make the loan the solution to that named problem, not a product pitch

- Secure a hard next step before ending the conversation
  - Offer two options: a 10-minute call to map the blocker-removal plan together, or a short intake form to pull a soft credit review now
  - Set the re-contact date explicitly: 'I'll follow up with you on [specific date] to check progress — does that work?'
  - Do not go silent after one exchange — schedule the next touch before this one ends
